script: Most iconic UNVEILINGS in football history. Real Madrid once paid ninety-four million euros for Cristiano Ronaldo, making him the most expensive footballer who had ever lived, and he was arriving from Manchester United as a Ballon d'Or winner. So the club threw him a presentation ceremony at the Santiago Bernabeu. But the size of the crowd that showed up is where this stops being a normal signing. On the sixth of July, 2009, eighty thousand fans packed the stadium just to watch one man walk onto a green carpet and kick a ball around for ten minutes, even though he hadn't played a single game yet. One journalist described the night as part coronation, part papal mass, and a dash of rock concert thrown in. And fans even stormed the pitch as Ronaldo told the crowd this was the completion of his boyhood dream. And here's the wild part, because eighty thousand people showing up for a guy in a suit was a bigger crowd than Real Madrid pulled for a lot of their actual matches that season. But the record he quietly set that night is the detail that still stuns people today. That eighty thousand broke a mark that had stood for twenty-five years, back when seventy-five thousand fans welcomed Diego Maradona to Napoli. And here's the part that gets people, because it's been more than fifteen years and no unveiling on earth has beaten it. When Real Madrid presented Kylian Mbappe in 2024, the whole world assumed he'd crush the record, and he didn't, since he only managed to tie it.
